content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"CORE_ONLY","rationale":"The book's core identification — that 'gospel' denotes the herald's proclamation of God's reign (the gospel of the kingdom), with the cross and resurrection functioning as the act that secures and enthrones the King rather than as the whole content of the announcement — is better supported by the supplied evidence than the strict kerygma-only definition. The book explains the data the counter must strain to accommodate: (1) the only content-title the gospel ever wears in the KJV is 'the gospel of the kingdom' (Matt 4:23; 24:14), never a title of death or cross; (2) Jesus, John, and the disciples preached and commanded belief in 'the gospel' years before the crucifixion, while the twelve did not yet understand the coming death (Mark 1:14-15; Luke 18:34) — impossible if the gospel's content just is the death-and-resurrection report; (3) Heb 4:2 says the gospel was preached to the wilderness generation and Gal 3:8 says it was pre-preached to Abraham, requiring content broader than the Christ-event report; (4) Rev 14:6-7's 'everlasting gospel' states its own content as fear-God/worship-the-Creator/judgment kingdom proclamation; (5) Isa 52:7, which Paul himself cites as gospel-preaching in Rom 10:15, compresses the message to 'Thy God reigneth'; (6) the New Testament speaks of 'obeying' the gospel (Rom 10:16; 2 Thess 1:8; 1 Pet 4:17), which fits a royal proclamation with terms, not a bare factual bulletin. The book also gives a coherent, non-evasive reading of the counter's strongest texts: 1 Cor 15:1-4 is doubly anchored 'according to the scriptures' and defends the resurrection as the gospel's hinge, and Rom 1:1-4 frames Paul's gospel in explicitly Davidic-enthronement terms. However, only the core survives scrutiny: the secondary elaborations — the chadash 'renewed covenant' etymology, the identification of the gospel's content with the Torah as such ('the law going forth from Zion,' Isa 2:3, which contains no gospel vocabulary), and the appeals to Hebrew Matthew and a Hebrew Revelation 'gilyon' — rest on weaker or unverifiable steps and are not needed for the core identification. Notably, the kingdom-centered reading is itself listed as a common scholarly position in both Response A and Response B, and Response B's primary meaning already fuses reign and Christ-event, confirming the counter is best construed as a narrower emphasis on the same referent rather than a contradictory rival.","book_core_identification":"The gospel is the proclamation of God's kingdom/reign — 'Thy God reigneth' (Isa 52:7) — an everlasting announcement carrying covenant terms, preached to Abraham, at Sinai, by Jesus before the cross, and to the end of the age, with Christ's death and resurrection as the act that secures the kingdom and enthrones the King rather than the entire content of the message.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The 'new covenant' is a renewed covenant based on the Hebrew root chadash meaning renew/repair, so the covenant terms (the Torah) are unchanged and only relocated to the heart (Jer 31:33)","The gospel is identified with the law itself going forth from Zion (Isa 2:3; Mic 4:2)","Believing the gospel equals obeying the King (Rom 10:16 obey/believe parallel; John 3:36)","Hebrew Matthew readings of Matt 23:2-3 ('all that he [Moses] says') and of the Great Commission ('forever'), including the taqqanot distinction","Hebrew Revelation's gilyon (stone tablet) behind the 'everlasting gospel' of Rev 14:6","Dating of the 'acceptable year' to the Day of Atonement AD 29","The claim that 'fulfil' (pleroo) in Matt 5:17 means to preach the law in its fullness rather than to complete and retire it"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream kerygma reading: 'gospel' is the technical term for the apostolic proclamation that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, was buried, and rose the third day, God's power for salvation to everyone who believes (1 Cor 15:1-4; Rom 1:16-17; Gal 1:6-9). On this view Jesus' pre-cross kingdom preaching is anticipatory announcement of what the cross would accomplish, Gal 3:8 and Heb 4:2 describe the gospel preached in promissory form, and the death-resurrection content is the settled definitional center once the events occur.","counter_core_identification":"The gospel is the good news of salvation accomplished through the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ, received by faith.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_NARROWER","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that the gospel's defining content is the arrival of God's reign with its covenant terms, asserting instead that the gospel is constituted by the Christ-event itself (death and resurrection for sin), such that anything preached before the cross was at most promise or anticipation of the gospel rather than the gospel proper.","counter_case":["1 Cor 15:1-4 is Paul's explicit self-described definition: 'I declare unto you the gospel which I preached... that Christ died for our sins... was buried... rose again the third day'","Rom 1:16-17 ties the gospel directly to salvation for everyone who believes, with righteousness by faith as its content","Gal 1:6-9 insists on one fixed gospel not to be altered, and Paul's gospel in his letters is centered on the crucified and risen Christ (1 Cor 2:2)","Eph 1:13 calls it 'the gospel of your salvation'","Gal 3:8 uses a distinct compound (proeuangelizomai, 'preached before the gospel'), which can be read as marking Abraham's case as anticipatory promise rather than the gospel itself","Heb 4:2 can be read as the promise of entering God's rest proclaimed to the wilderness generation, a type of the later gospel, not identical content"],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Explains the exclusive content-title 'gospel of the kingdom' (Matt 4:23; 9:35; 24:14) and the absence of any title referencing death, cross, or forgiveness","Explains how Jesus could command hearers to 'believe the gospel' (Mark 1:15) years before the cross while the disciples 'understood none of these things' about His death (Luke 18:34)","Explains Heb 4:2 and Gal 3:8 as literal statements of one everlasting gospel rather than requiring an anticipatory/promissory workaround","Explains Rev 14:6-7, where the 'everlasting gospel' states its content as fear God, give glory, worship the Creator, judgment — kingdom-herald content with no mention of the cross","Explains Paul's citation of Isa 52:7 ('Thy God reigneth') as gospel-preaching in Rom 10:15, linking euangelizo directly to the reign-announcement of basar","Explains the 'obey the gospel' texts (Rom 10:16; 2 Thess 1:8; 1 Pet 4:17), which fit a royal proclamation with covenant terms better than a factual report","Explains Rom 1:1-4's framing of Paul's gospel in Davidic enthronement language ('promised afore by his prophets... seed of David... declared Son of God with power by the resurrection')","Accommodates 1 Cor 15:1-4 without contradiction, reading it as the hinge (accession of the King) doubly anchored 'according to the scriptures,' while Matt 24:14 shows the end-time gospel still titled 'of the kingdom'"],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["1 Cor 15:1-4 uses explicit definitional language ('I declare unto you the gospel') centered on death, burial, resurrection","Rom 1:16 and Eph 1:13 connect the gospel most directly to personal salvation by faith","The apostolic preaching in Acts consistently climaxes in the death and resurrection (Acts 10:36-43), suggesting the Christ-event is the operative center of the proclaimed message","The distinct compound in Gal 3:8 gives lexical grounds for treating pre-Christ gospel references as anticipatory rather than identical in content"],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Isaiah 52:7 with Romans 10:15 (Paul cites the 'Thy God reigneth' herald-verse as gospel-preaching)","Mark 1:14-15 and Matthew 4:23 (the gospel of the kingdom preached and commanded to be believed before the cross)","Matthew 24:14 (the end-time message still titled 'this gospel of the kingdom')","Hebrews 4:2 (the gospel preached to the wilderness generation)","Galatians 3:8 (the gospel preached before to Abraham)","Revelation 14:6-7 (the everlasting gospel's stated content is Creator-worship and judgment)","Romans 10:16; 2 Thessalonians 1:8; 1 Peter 4:17 (the gospel as something obeyed)","Romans 1:1-4 (Paul's gospel framed as Davidic enthronement)"],"unresolved_objections":["The chadash 'renewed not new' covenant argument is contestable: Heb 8:13 says 'in that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old,' and chadash/kainos can denote genuine newness; the etymological argument from Psalm 51 and 2 Chronicles does not settle Jeremiah 31's sense","The identification of the gospel with the law itself ('the law going forth from Zion,' Isa 2:3) exceeds the evidence: Isa 2:3 contains no gospel/basar vocabulary, and equating the proclamation with the Torah as its content is a further step beyond 'the kingdom carries covenant terms'","The Hebrew Matthew (Matt 23:2-3 'all that he says'; the 'forever' in the commission) and Hebrew Revelation gilyon readings rest on disputed textual traditions not established by the supplied evidence","The reading of pleroo in Matt 5:17 as 'preach in fullness' rather than 'bring to fulfillment/completion' is one contested lexical option among several","Heb 4:2 can plausibly be read as the promise of rest proclaimed in typological form, so it supports but does not by itself compel the one-everlasting-gospel identification"],"confidence":"medium"}
